headline: Benchmarking and patient-level models refine scRNA-seq imputation and stratification
label: Single Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Methods
summary: Recent benchmarks test whether complex models outperform simpler approaches across imputation, deconvolution, and patient stratification.
synthesis: The common thread is evaluation of analytical choices against alternatives in single-cell and bulk transcriptomics. A 15-method scRNA-seq imputation benchmark across 30 datasets and 6 downstream analyses reports that traditional methods often outperform deep learning approaches. An 11-cohort benchmark finds that CLR-transformed cell-type proportions match or beat complex sample representations for unsupervised patient stratification. Other items build methods that account for biological structure: PaSCient builds patient-level embeddings from multi-cellular contexts; BLUE, a U-Net, deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific profiles; DeConveil uses CNV-aware negative binomial GLMs for aneuploid cancer genomes; and tnQTL mapping in iPSC-derived midbrain scRNA-seq from 155 individuals links transcriptional noise to schizophrenia GWAS signals. What is new is the joint emphasis on benchmarking against alternatives and on accounting for composition, dosage, and noise.
